# Mike Basios

> Mike (Michail) Basios builds optimisation systems that improve code, models and agents under measurement, in production for nine years: co-founder and CTO of TurinTech AI (London, UCL spinout), designer of Artemis and builder of the first version of its Discovery engine, an optimisation platform that combines evolutionary search with multi-LLM orchestration to improve code, models and AI agents under measurement. PhD from University College London on Darwinian code optimisation; ACM GECCO Human-Competitive Results (Humies) Bronze Award 2019.

Key facts:
- Name: Michail Basios, usually Mike Basios. Published as "Michail Basios" or "Mike Basios".
- Role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, TurinTech AI (Turing Intelligence Technology Ltd), since 2017. Based in London, UK.
- Own contribution: the original research and paper on Darwinian data-structure selection that Artemis grew out of; the design of the Artemis system; the first version of Discovery. On later papers: the research hypothesis and the design of the experiments, with the TurinTech team doing the rest.
- Built: Artemis, TurinTech's AI optimisation platform, and Discovery, its mode that systematically tests hundreds of optimisation approaches against the real workload and ranks them by measured effect. Artemis-found optimisations have been merged upstream by the maintainers of NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp and OpenAI Whisper, among others (see https://www.turintech.ai/open-source).
- Earlier product: evoML, TurinTech's evolutionary AutoML studio (Computing Technology Product Awards, AI Product of the Year 2022).
- Education: BSc Informatics, University of Piraeus (first class); MSc Computer Science, University of Edinburgh (with distinction); began research at Edinburgh, then moved the PhD to University College London, supervised by Earl Barr with Ilya Sergey (thesis "Darwinian code optimisation", January 2019: https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10070648/ ; PDF https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10070648/1/Basios_10070648_thesis.pdf). The thesis introduced Darwinian Data Structures and the first Artemis, a cloud-based multi-objective, multi-language optimiser that rewrote the data structures of 44 programs (median 4.8% runtime, 10.1% memory, 5.1% CPU improvement), plus Proteus, a framework for upgradeable Ethereum smart contracts.
- Interests: autoresearch (AI systems that run their own research loop: hypothesise, experiment, measure, keep what works), recursive self-improvement, self-learning systems, and meta systems (systems that improve the systems that improve the code). Artemis Discovery is a production version of that loop; the work on evolving LLM-based agents extends it into a meta system.
- Research: search-based and evolutionary software optimisation, genetic improvement, LLM-guided search for code optimisation, optimisation of LLM-based agents. Papers at ESEC/FSE, ICSE, ASE, SSBSE, IEEE CAI, IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence. 1,100+ citations, h-index 10 (Google Scholar, September 2026).
- Teaching and supervision: lab teaching for the Extreme Computing course (Hadoop, Spark) at the University of Edinburgh; MSc thesis and project supervision at UCL, often as industry internships; co-supervision of PhD students working on TurinTech research problems; collaborations with researchers at UCL, Leeds (Innovate UK Knowledge Transfer Partnership), Surrey, King's College London and Warwick; Horizon 2020 grant.
- Contact: mike@turintech.ai
